''' Jennifer {{Nobold|"}}Jenny{{Nobold|"}} Eve Hoffman''' is an American physicist and a professor at [[Harvard University]]. Hoffman is interested in atomic-scale synthesis and imaging of quantum materials, using [[molecular beam epitaxy]] and [[scanning probe microscopy]]. Hoffman has received several awards for her research and teaching, including the 2005 [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers]]<ref>[ftp://ftp.csr.utexas.edu/pub/ggfc/misc/PECASE PR Release.pdf "White House Announces 2005 Awards for Early Career Scientists and Engineers"]{{Dead link|date=February 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} (PDF). Office of Science and Technology Policy, Executive Office of the President. 2006-07-26. Retrieved 2018-11-12 – via Center for Space Research, University of Texas at Austin.</ref> and 2010 [[Sloan Research Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sloan.org/past-fellows|title=Past Fellows|website=sloan.org|access-date=2019-03-06|archive-date=2018-03-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180314000756/https://sloan.org/past-fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Education ==
After graduating from [[Greenwich Academy]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laguarda |first=Ignacio |date=2026-05-21 |title=Greenwich Academy holds graduation ceremony for Class of 2026 as a light rain falls |url=https://www.greenwichtime.com/news/education/article/greenwich-academy-graduation-ceremony-class-2026-22266656.php |access-date=2026-05-22 |website=Greenwich Time |language=en}}</ref> Hoffman went on to study physics at [[Harvard University]], earning a [[A.B.|B.A.]] with ''[[magna cum laude]]'' distinction in 1999. She then entered the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where she obtained an [[M.A.]] in 2001, and a [[Ph.D.]] in 2003. While a graduate student of UC Berkeley, Hoffman worked with [[J. C. Séamus Davis]] on the characterization of [[bismuth strontium calcium copper oxide]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://users.physics.harvard.edu/~jhoffman/index.php|title=Jenny Hoffman|website=users.physics.harvard.edu|access-date=2018-06-02|archive-date=2017-09-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912105207/http://users.physics.harvard.edu/~jhoffman/index.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> which became the topic of her doctoral thesis.<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Hoffman|first=Jennifer Eve|year=2003|title=A Search for Alternative Electronic Order in the High Temperature Superconductor Bi{{Sub|2}}Sr{{Sub|2}}CaCu{{Sub|2}}O{{Sub|8+δ}} by Scanning Tunneling Microscopy|url=https://davis-group-quantum-matter-research.ie/theses/Thesis_JennyHoffman.pdf|degree=Ph.D.}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
Hoffman joined [[Stanford University]] as a postdoctoral research associate in [[Kathryn Moler]]'s group.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://web.stanford.edu/group/moler/people.html|title=Moler Group Members|last=Inc.|first=CoffeeCup Software|website=web.stanford.edu|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref> In 2005, she joined [[Harvard University]] as an assistant professor. Hoffman's group use [[layer by layer]] growth and high-resolution imaging of molecules.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://hoffman.physics.harvard.edu/research.php|title=Jenny Hoffman Lab Research Scanning Tunneling Microscopy|website=hoffman.physics.harvard.edu|access-date=2018-06-02|archive-date=2018-06-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612183417/http://hoffman.physics.harvard.edu/research.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> Using [[scanning tunneling spectroscopy]] they explained vortex pinning in [[High-temperature superconductivity|high-temperature superconductors]].<ref name=":0" /> She is also interested in [[topological insulator]]s and [[strongly correlated material]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cifar.ca/profiles/jennifer-hoffman/|title=Jennifer Hoffman - CIFAR : CIFAR|website=www.cifar.ca|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-02}}{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>  She has won several large research grants, from [[National Science Foundation]], the [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]], [[Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation]], [[United States – Israel Binational Science Foundation]] and the [[Air Force Research Laboratory]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.harvard.edu/node/399|title=Hoffman, Kim, Yacoby receive 2014 Moore Foundation Experimental Investigator Award in Emergent Phenomena in Quantum Systems {{!}} Harvard University Department of Physics|website=www.physics.harvard.edu|access-date=2018-06-02|archive-date=2018-09-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180909035601/https://www.physics.harvard.edu/node/399|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://hoffman.physics.harvard.edu/funding.php|title=Hoffman Lab Funding|website=hoffman.physics.harvard.edu|access-date=2018-06-02|archive-date=2018-05-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180528221655/http://hoffman.physics.harvard.edu/funding.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> She has developed [[quasiparticle interference imaging]] and force microscopy to trigger electronic phase transitions.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.seas.harvard.edu/directory/jhoffman|title=Jenny Hoffman|date=2017-11-23|website=www.seas.harvard.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref>

In 2015, Hoffman joined [[University of British Columbia]] as a Canada Excellence Research Chair.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ubyssey.ca/features/fresh-from-harvard-jenny-hoffman-adjusts-to-ubc/|title=Our Campus: Fresh from Harvard, hotshot prof Jenny Hoffman adjusts to Point Grey|work=The Ubyssey|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref> The position was worth $10 million over seven years, enabling [[University of British Columbia]] to use atomic level 3D printing.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://vancouversun.com/technology/Renowned+Harvard+quantum+physicist+joining/11170772/story.html|title=Renowned Harvard quantum physicist joining UBC|last=Bellett|first=Gerry|work=www.vancouversun.com|access-date=2018-06-02|language=en-ca|archive-date=2016-09-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160928062124/http://www.vancouversun.com/technology/renowned+harvard+quantum+physicist+joining/11170772/story.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://globalnews.ca/video/2085910/renowned-quantum-physicist-jennifer-hoffman-comes-to-bc|title=Renowned quantum physicist Jennifer Hoffman comes to BC {{!}} Watch News Videos Online|website=Global News|language=en|access-date=2018-06-02|archive-date=2015-07-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150703065550/http://globalnews.ca/video/2085910/renowned-quantum-physicist-jennifer-hoffman-comes-to-bc|url-status=dead}}</ref> She returned to [[Harvard University]] after less than a year.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/technology/science/quantum-materials-research-chair-leaves-ubc-after-less-than-a-year/article29600035/|title=Quantum materials research chair leaves UBC after less than a year|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2013, the [[Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study]] awarded her a fellowship to image complex oxides.<ref name=":1" />

== Athletics ==
As an undergraduate at Harvard University, Hoffman rowed on the varsity crew team (lightweight). In her senior year, she began to run marathons, and has since taken up triathlons and [[Ultramarathon|ultramarathons.]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://users.physics.harvard.edu/~jhoffman/adventure.php?showthumbs=CompleteRaceList|title=Jenny Hoffman Adventures|website=users.physics.harvard.edu|access-date=2018-06-02|archive-date=2014-12-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228215100/http://users.physics.harvard.edu/~jhoffman/adventure.php?showthumbs=CompleteRaceList|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Hoffman won the national title in the USA Track & Field National Championship 24 Hour Run in 2014, 2015 and 2016,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.usaultrarunning.com/24-hour-team/|title=24 Hour Team {{!}} USA Ultra Running|website=www.usaultrarunning.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-06-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.physics.harvard.edu/node/695|title=Hoffman Wins in USA Track & Field National Championship 24 Hour Run! {{!}} Harvard University Department of Physics|website=www.physics.harvard.edu|access-date=2018-06-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202115656/https://www.physics.harvard.edu/node/695|archive-date=2017-02-02|url-status=dead}}</ref> and she was selected as the USATF athlete of the week in September 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.legacy.usatf.org/News/Hoffman-s-three-peat-at-USATF-24-Hour-Championship.aspx|title=USATF Athlete of the Week|date=23 September 2016}}</ref> She competed on the gold medal-winning team at the IAU 24 Hour World Championships in Belfast, UK in July 2017.

In November 2023, Hoffman set a new record for the fastest known time for a woman to run across the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Milne |first=Keeley |date=2023-11-09 |title=Harvard physics professor destroys transamerica speed record |url=https://runningmagazine.ca/the-scene/harvard-physics-professor-destroys-transamerica-speed-record/ |access-date=2023-11-12 |website=Canadian Running Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lim |first=Megan |date=2023-11-10 |title=This physics professor ran 3,000 miles across America in record time |work=National Public Radio |url=https://www.npr.org/2023/11/10/1212383938/running-marathon-record-jenny-hoffman}}</ref> She completed the [[Trans America Run]] from [[San Francisco]] to [[New York City]], covering 3,032 miles, in 47 days, 12 hours, and 35 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |title=FKT: Jenny Hoffman - Trans America Run (USA) |url=https://fastestknowntime.com/fkt/jenny-hoffman-trans-america-run-usa-2023-11-02 |website=Fastest Known Time |date=16 September 2023 |access-date=17 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Atwal |first1=Sanj |title=Harvard professor runs across America in record-breaking time |url=https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/news/2024/4/harvard-professor-runs-across-america-in-record-breaking-time-768822 |publisher=Guinness World Records |access-date=17 September 2024}}</ref>

== Personal records ==
* [[Marathon]] - 3:23:08 (Lowell, MA, 2021)
* 100 Miles - 15:26:51 (Milwaukee, WI, 2023)
* [[24 hours run|24 Hour]] - 147.7673 miles (Milwaukee, WI, 2024)
* [[Trans America Run]] - 47 days, 12 hours, 35 minutes (SF to NY, 2023)
